results.question: what is the notice period?
results.answer: The notice period for employees within their first year of confirmed service is 30 days. For employees with more than one year of confirmed service, the notice period is 60 days. Notice must be provided in writing and can be served via email to hr@turabitsolutions.com, with confirmation in writing. For senior roles, the notice period is extended to 60 calendar days. The company may waive the notice period and pay salary in lieu of notice. Termination for cause may occur without notice. Resignation requires serving the specified notice period, and failure to do so may result in recovery of equivalent salary from the employee's final settlement.

## Termination Conditions, Notice Period and Severance
Either party may terminate this employment by providing written notice to the other party. For employees within their first year of confirmed service, the notice period is 30 days. For employees with more than one year of confirmed service, the notice period is 60 days. Notice may be served via email to hr@turabitsolutions.com and must be confirmed in writing. The company reserves the right to waive the notice period and instead pay salary in lieu of notice. Termination for cause, including but not limited to gross misconduct, fraud, theft, breach of confidentiality, willful insubordination, conviction of a criminal offence, or sustained poor performance after a formal performance improvement plan, may be effected without notice or severance. Termination without cause requires payment of salary in lieu of notice. Resignation by the employee requires written notice as specified; failure to serve the notice period entitles the company to recover the equivalent salary from the employee's full and final settlement. Upon termination for any reason, the employee must return all company property on the last working day. Full and final settlement will be processed within 45 days of the last working day. No contractual severance beyond statutory obligations applies unless specifically agreed in writing at the time of separation.

## Separation Policy and Exit Process
Employees shall provide a written resignation notice of at least 30 calendar days prior to their intended last working day. For senior roles, this notice period shall be extended to 60 calendar days. The company reserves the right to initiate termination by providing a minimum of 30 calendar days' notice or payment in lieu of notice, except in cases involving gross misconduct, where immediate termination may occur without notice.
Upon separation, employees must complete a formal exit process which includes the thorough transfer of knowledge and responsibilities to designated colleagues or successors. All company property, including but not limited to hardware, software, access cards, and confidential documents, shall be returned in good condition before the final clearance is granted. Access to company systems and networks shall be revoked promptly upon the employee's last working day.
The full and final settlement of all dues, including salary, bonuses, and any applicable reimbursements, shall be processed and paid within 45 calendar days following the employee's last working day. An experience letter confirming the period of employment and role shall be issued within seven working days after the completion of the exit clearance process.
Employees must comply fully with these separation obligations to ensure a smooth transition and maintain the integrity of Turabit Solutions' operations. Failure to adhere to these requirements may delay final settlements or affect the issuance of employment verification documents. The company expects all departing employees to uphold the same standards of professionalism and integrity during the exit process as demonstrated throughout their tenure.

## Notice Period Buyout and Early Release Conditions
Turabit solutions recognizes that circumstances may arise where an employee requests early release from their notice period or wishes to buy out the remaining notice period. Such requests shall be considered on a case-by-case basis, balancing the employee's needs with the company's operational requirements.
Employees seeking early release must submit a formal written request to Human Resources, detailing the reasons for the request and the proposed last working day. The company shall evaluate the impact of the early release on ongoing projects, team capacity, and knowledge transfer obligations before making a decision.
Notice period buyout involves the employee compensating the company for the unserved portion of the notice period. The buyout amount is calculated based on the employee's gross salary for the remaining notice days. This amount must be paid in full before the employee's last working day, and the company will provide a formal invoice for the same.
Approval of early release or notice period buyout is at the sole discretion of the company and requires written confirmation from Human Resources and the employee's reporting manager. If approved, the employee must complete all clearance formalities and knowledge transfer activities before departure.
In cases where early release or buyout is not approved, the employee is expected to serve the full notice period as per policy. Non-compliance may affect the issuance of relieving documents and final settlement processing.

results.question: what are the leave policies?
results.answer: Turabit Solutions' leave policies provide employees with 12 earned leave days annually, accruing monthly, with a carry forward limit of 6 days into the next year. Additionally, employees receive 6 casual or sick leave days per year, which are non-cumulative and must be used within the calendar year. The company observes 12 designated public holidays annually. Leave requests must be submitted through the Human Resource Management System (HRMS) with at least two days' advance notice for planned absences. Attendance is monitored via biometric systems and remote check-ins. More than three unexplained absences in a quarter trigger a formal review. Failure to comply with leave procedures may result in disciplinary action. Earned Leave can be encashed only during annual encashment in November or upon separation, with specific conditions and limits. Sick, Casual, Compensatory Off, and statutory leaves are not eligible for encashment. These policies align with legal frameworks such as the Factories Act 1948, Shops and Establishments Act (Maharashtra) 2017, Maternity Benefit Act 1961, Payment of Gratuity Act 1972, and Code on Social Security 2020, ensuring compliance and fairness.
contexts:
## Purpose and Legal Basis
The leave policy at Turabit solutions is designed to provide employees with a structured, fair, and predictable framework for taking time off. This supports their health, personal obligations, and overall work-life balance while ensuring that business operations continue smoothly without disruption. By standardizing leave entitlements across the organization, the policy reduces ad-hoc leave requests and promotes consistent decision-making by managers. This consistency helps maintain fairness and transparency in leave management.
The policy is grounded in applicable legal frameworks including the Factories Act 1948, Shops and Establishments Act (Maharashtra) 2017, Maternity Benefit Act 1961, Payment of Gratuity Act 1972, and relevant provisions of the Code on Social Security 2020. These laws provide the statutory foundation for various leave types and entitlements, ensuring compliance with national labor standards.
By aligning company leave practices with these legal requirements, Turabit solutions ensures that employee rights are protected while balancing organizational needs. The policy also clarifies the roles and responsibilities of employees, managers, and HR in the leave application and approval process, fostering a culture of accountability and mutual respect.

## Leave and Attendance Policy Summary
Employees shall be entitled to a total of 12earned leave days annually, which shall accrue on a monthly basis. Earned leave may be carried forward up to a maximum of 6 days into the following year. In addition, employees shall receive 6 casual or sick leave days per year, which are non-cumulative and must be utilized within the calendar year. The company recognizes twelve designated public holidays each year, which employees shall observe in accordance with the official holiday calendar.
All leave requests must be submitted through the Human Resource Management System (HRMS) with a minimum of two days' advance notice for planned absences. Attendance shall be monitored through biometric systems and remote check-in procedures to ensure accurate tracking. Employees must maintain regular attendance and provide valid explanations for any absences. Should an employee incur more than three unexplained absences within a single quarter, a formal review process shall be initiated to address the issue.
It is the obligation of every employee to adhere strictly to these leave and attendance requirements to maintain operational efficiency and team coordination. Failure to comply with the leave request procedures or attendance policies may result in disciplinary action as outlined in the company's disciplinary process. Employees are expected to plan their leave responsibly, ensuring minimal disruption to their work and team commitments.
Turabit Solutions shall enforce these policies consistently to uphold fairness and transparency across all departments. Employees shall remain responsible for monitoring their leave balances and ensuring compliance with the company's attendance standards. The Human Resources department shall provide support and guidance regarding leave entitlements and attendance tracking as needed.

## Employee Benefits
At Turabit Solutions, we recognize that our employees are our most valuable asset, and we are committed to providing a comprehensive benefits package that supports your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Our benefits are designed to reflect our core values of ownership, customer focus, and continuous improvement, ensuring that you feel valued and empowered as part of our team.
Health and insurance coverage are key components of our benefits. We provide a group mediclaim policy with coverage of Rs 3 lakh per year for employees, along with an additional Rs 2 lakh coverage for one dependent. In addition, the company offers term life insurance at no cost to you, providing financial security for you and your family.
Leave entitlements are structured to support your personal and professional needs. You are entitled to 12 days of earned leave annually, which accrues monthly and can be carried forward up to 6 days. Additionally, you receive six casual or sick leave days each year, which are not carried forward. The company observes 12 public holidays per year. All leave requests should be submitted through the HR Management System with a minimum of two days' advance notice for planned absences. Attendance is monitored via biometric systems and remote check-ins, and any unexplained absences exceeding three days in a quarter will prompt a formal review.
To encourage continuous learning and professional development, each employee is allocated an annual learning budget of Rs 15,000. This budget can be used for courses, certifications, or other approved educational activities that enhance your skills and contribute to your growth within the company.
Our salary structure is designed to reward performance and align with company goals. Your total cost to company (CTC) includes a fixed base salary comprising 60%, a performance bonus of up to 20% paid quarterly based on individual KPIs and company revenue targets, a special allowance, and provident fund contributions. Salaries are credited on the 28th of each month, or on the preceding working day if the 28th falls on a weekend or public holiday.
For employees who have completed five years of continuous service, gratuity benefits are provided in accordance with the Payment of Gratuity Act, recognizing your long-term commitment to Turabit Solutions.
We believe that these benefits, combined with our culture of ownership, directness, and customer obsession, create a supportive environment where you can thrive. Should you have any questions about your benefits or require assistance, please reach out to the Human Resources team. Your well-being and professional development are priorities for us as we work together to achieve our mission of building reliable, scalable SaaS products that empower mid-market businesses across South and Southeast Asia.

## Leave Encashment Policy and Conditions
Earned Leave (EL) encashment is permitted only in two scenarios: at the time of full and final settlement upon employee separation, and during the annual encashment window held in November each year.
Upon separation, all accumulated Earned Leave up to the 24-day cap shall be encashed at the rate calculated as (Basic Salary divided by 26) multiplied by the number of days encashed.
During the annual encashment window, employees may encash up to six Earned Leave days if their balance exceeds 12 days.
Encashment payments are subject to tax deduction at source as applicable under prevailing tax laws.
Sick Leave, Casual Leave, Compensatory Off, and statutory leaves are not eligible for encashment under any circumstances.
Employees must apply for annual encashment within the specified window; late applications will not be entertained.
The company reserves the right to verify leave balances and eligibility before processing encashment payments.
Encashment shall not affect the employee's leave accrual or carry forward entitlements except as explicitly stated in this policy.
